We have mass spec: m/z 179.0946 (intensity 100). Likely molecular ion [M+H]+? Usually ESI positive gives [M+H]+. So M = 178.0946? Actually m/z 179.0946 likely corresponds to C10H13NO2? Let's calculate exact mass: C10H13NO2: C10=120.000, H13=13.101, N=14.003, O2=31.989 => total 179.093. Yes matches. So molecular formula C10H13NO2 (neutral). The proton NMR shows: 2.58 t (2H), 2.84 t (2H), 3.81 s (3H), aromatic 7.17 ddd (2H), 7.93 ddd (2H). So aromatic AA'BB' pattern typical of para-disubstituted benzene. Two doublets of doublet of doublet? but 2H each. So para-disubstituted aromatic ring.

Signals: 3.81 singlet 3H likely methoxy OCH3. Aromatic 4 protons suggests para-disubstituted phenyl with electron-withdrawing/donating groups.

Two aliphatic triplets each 2H at 2.58 and 2.84, J=7.4 Hz typical ethyl chain CH2-CH2 attached to carbonyl? Possibly CH2-CH2 attached to carbonyl and aromatic? For example, phenethyl acetate? But we have OCH3 also.

We have formula C10H13NO2 includes N. So maybe N-methyl? Wait OCH3 is 3H, plus aromatic 4H, plus two CH2 groups (4H) total 11H, plus maybe NH? But we have 13 H total. OCH3 (3), aromatic (4), two CH2 (4) =11, remaining 2 H maybe on N (NH2) or CH? But N present.

Consider structure: para-methoxy phenyl attached to carbonyl? For example, p-anisoyl? p-anisic acid is C8H8O3. Not match.

Our N maybe part of amide: e.g., p-anisamide (p-methoxybenzamide) formula C8? Actually p-anisamide: C8? Let's compute: C8? Wait anisamide: C8? Actually anisamide = p-methoxybenzamide: C8? Let's compute: C8? No, benzamide C7H7NO, plus OCH3 adds C1H3O => C8H10NO2? Actually benzamide C7H7NO, plus OCH3 on para gives C8H9NO2? Let's compute: C7H7NO + OCH3 (C1H3O) = C8H10NO2? Wait need to add OCH3 to ring replacing H, so formula C8? Starting benzamide C7H7NO? Actually benzamide is C7H7NO? No benzamide is C7H7NO? Let's check: C6H5CONH2 = C7H7NO? plus O? Actually CONH2 adds C1 O1 N1 H2, so total C7H7NO? plus O? Wait carbonyl O is included. So C7H7NO? plus O? I'm confused.

Better compute: C6H5 (phenyl) + C(=O)NH2 => C7H7NO? plus O? carbonyl O is O, so C7H7NO? Actually formula C7H7NO? includes O? Should be C7H7NO? but need O2? Let's check: C6H5 + C(=O)NH2 = C7H7NO? plus O? The carbonyl O is part of C=O, so O1. So total O1. So benzamide C7H7NO? Actually known formula of benzamide is C7H7NO? Wait actual benzamide formula is C7H7NO? Let's quickly recall: benzamide C7H7NO? I think it's C7H7NO? but I think it's C7H7NO? plus O? Actually benzamide is C7H7NO? I'm not sure.

Anyway our formula C10H13NO2 suggests aromatic ring (C6H4) plus OCH3 (C1H3O) plus CH2-CH2-CO? Let's propose: p-methoxy phenyl attached to CH2-CH2-CO-NH? That would be 4+3+4+? Let's compute: aromatic C6H4 (para substituted) = C6H4. OCH3 = C1H3O. Two CH2 = C2H4. Carbonyl C=O = C1O1. N H? maybe NH? So total C =6+1+2+1=10. H =4+3+4+? N-H maybe 1? total 12? plus maybe extra H on N? Actually amide NH2 would add 2 H. But we have 13 H total. Let's compute: C6H4 (4 H), OCH3 (3 H) =>7, CH2-CH2 (4 H) =>11, NH? maybe NH? adds 1 =>12, plus maybe extra H on carbonyl? no. So need 13 H, maybe NH2 (2 H) gives 13. So structure: p-methoxy phenyl-CH2-CH2-CO-NH2? That's p-anisic acid amide? Actually that's 4-(methoxy)phenylpropionamide? Wait chain length: phenyl-CH2-CH2-CO-NH2 is phenethyl amide? That's phenethyl amide with methoxy substituent para. So formula: C6H4 (para) + OCH3 + CH2-CH2-CO-NH2. Let's compute: Carbons: aromatic 6, OCH3 1, CH2-CH2 2, carbonyl carbon 1 =10. Hydrogens: aromatic 4, OCH3 3 =7, CH2-CH2 4 =11, NH2 2 =13. O atoms: OCH3 (1), carbonyl O (1) =2. N 1. So matches C10H13NO2. Good.

Now NMR: CH2 adjacent to carbonyl (CH2-CO) would appear around 2.58 t? Actually CH2 next to carbonyl appears ~2.3-2.5. CH2 next to aromatic appears ~2.7-3.0. So we have two triplets 2.58 and 2.84, J=7.4, consistent with -CH2-CH2- chain. OCH3 singlet 3.81 (para methoxy). Aromatic protons: para-disubstituted gives AA'BB' pattern: two doublets, but here ddd due to meta coupling? But still 2H each at 7.17 and 7.93. That fits.

Thus structure is 4-methoxyphenethylamide (p-anisyl ethyl amide). SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)CC(=O)N? Wait chain: phenyl-CH2-CH2-CO-NH2. So SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)CC(=O)N. But need para substitution: COc1ccc(cc1)CC(=O)N. That is 4-methoxy phenethyl amide. Let's validate: "COc1ccc(cc1)CC(=O)N". Count atoms: C O? Let's compute formula: COc1ccc(cc1) = anisole ring: C7H7O? Actually anisole C7H8O? Wait anisole is C7H8O? Actually anisole C7H8O? but we have OCH3 attached to phenyl, so C7H8O? plus chain C2H4 + C=O + NH2. Let's compute: anisole part: C7H8O (C6H4 + OCH3). That's C7H8O. Add CH2-CH2-CO-NH2: C3H5NO? Actually CH2-CH2-CO-NH2 = C3H6NO? Let's compute: CH2-CH2 = C2H4, carbonyl C=O adds C1O1, NH2 adds N1H2. So total C3H6NO? plus O from carbonyl already counted. So overall C10H14NO2? Wait combine: C7H8O + C3H6NO = C10H14NO2? That's H14 not 13. But note anisole part includes OCH3 (3 H) and aromatic H4 =7 H? Actually anisole C7H8O includes 8 H (4 aromatic + 3 OCH3 + 1? Wait anisole C6H5-O-CH3: aromatic H5? Actually anisole has formula C7H8O, yes 8 H. In para-methoxy phenyl, we have 4 aromatic H (since para substitution reduces to 4). So anisole part with para substitution still C7H8O? The OCH3 adds 3 H, aromatic H4, total 7? plus maybe one extra? Let's compute: ring C6, substituents: OCH3 and CH2CH2CO... So aromatic hydrogens = 4. OCH3 = 3. So total H =7. So anisole part (C7) includes OCH3 and aromatic ring with 4 H, plus maybe one H on carbon attached to O? Actually OCH3 carbon has 3 H, O attached to ring carbon (no H). So total H = 4+3 =7. So C7H7O? Wait formula C7H7O? But anisole is C7H8O because anisole has 5 aromatic H (unsubstituted). Here we have para substitution, so one H replaced by chain, so C7H7O? Actually the ring carbon attached to chain is part of C7? The chain carbon is separate. So the aromatic ring carbon attached to chain loses H, so overall H count reduces by 1. So C7H7O (since OCH3 still 3 H, aromatic 4 H). So C7H7O. Then chain CH2-CH2-CO-NH2 adds C3H6NO? Let's compute: CH2-CH2 = C2H4, carbonyl C=O adds C1O1, NH2 adds N1H2. So total C3H6NO? plus O from carbonyl already counted. So combine: C7H7O + C3H6NO = C10H13NO2. Yes matches! Good.

Thus SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)CC(=O)N . Need para orientation: COc1ccc(cc1)CC(=O)N is para? Actually COc1ccc(cc1) is anisole with unspecified substitution pattern; the chain attaches at position 1? In SMILES, "COc1ccc(cc1)CC(=O)N" attaches chain at the same carbon as O? Wait "COc1ccc(cc1)" is anisole where OCH3 attached to aromatic carbon 1, and the rest of ring is unsubstituted. The chain "CC(=O)N" attached to the aromatic carbon after the ring closure? In SMILES, after the ring closure "c1", the next atoms are attached to the last aromatic carbon before closure. The pattern "c1ccc(cc1)C" attaches to the last aromatic carbon (position 4). So this gives para? Let's check: anisole: "COc1ccc(cc1)" OCH3 at position 1, chain attached at position 4 (para). So correct.
